key_insight: VINO unifies image and video generation/editing in one model by conditioning a single diffusion backbone on interleaved text, image, and video context, enabled by a vision-language model paired with a Multimodal Diffusion Transformer (MMDiT).
problem_solved: Eliminates the need for separate, modality-specific generators and editing modules by providing a single framework that handles mixed-modal inputs and outputs (text, images, videos) for both creation and editing tasks.
method: A shared diffusion backbone that accepts conditioning from multiple modalities (text, image, video) to produce images or video frames.
Coupling a vision-language model (VLM) with a Multimodal Diffusion Transformer (MMDiT) to encode interleaved omni-modal context and enable cross-modal attention.
Unified training/inference pipeline that supports generation and editing across modalities without separate task-specific modules.
impact: Simplifies deployment and workflows by providing one model for diverse visual creation/editing tasks, improving consistency across modalities and reducing engineering overhead for multimodal applications.
visual_elements: Architectural diagram: VLM + MMDiT feeding a shared diffusion backbone, with arrows for text/image/video conditioning.
Input→Output pipeline: examples showing text+image prompts producing edited images and videos (before/after).
Comparison chart: single unified model vs. separate modality models (metrics like latency, parameter count, cross-modal consistency).
Qualitative grid: side-by-side generated images and video frames highlighting multimodal conditioning effects.
paper_title: VINO: A Unified Visual Generator with Interleaved OmniModal Context
paper_authors: Junyi Chen, Tong He, Zhoujie Fu, Pengfei Wan, Kun Gai
